eventMetadata.context_description:
**Current NWS forecasts for Houston on August 16, 2026, call for sunny skies and a high near 96°F**, which aligns with the market's leading 96-97°F bin at 48.5% implied probability. Typical mid-August climatology features daily highs of 93–95°F, with rare exceedances above 100°F; the current setup reflects a continuation of hot, stable high-pressure conditions with minimal cloud cover or precipitation to suppress temperatures.

Model consensus and recent observations emphasize clear to mostly sunny conditions, allowing strong daytime heating under high sun angles and light winds. Humidity remains elevated, but actual air temperature readings (not heat index) depend primarily on insolation and boundary-layer mixing rather than moisture. No significant frontal passages, tropical moisture surges, or sea-breeze enhancements are expected to cap highs below the mid-90s or push them into the upper 90s to 100°F range in the metro area.

Traders appear to be weighting the official forecast high most heavily while assigning modest probability to slight under- or over-performance due to local microclimate variations or last-minute model adjustments. The next relevant data points will be afternoon observations and any updated NWS or mesoscale model runs through the peak heating hours.
